title: Haunting Ground
subtitle: An escape shared with a dog

body: Haunting Ground is Capcom's PlayStation 2 survival horror game, first released in Japan on 21 April 2005. Fiona Belli wakes inside an unfamiliar castle after a car accident and tries to find a way out. She frees a white shepherd named Hewie, whose help becomes essential as the inhabitants pursue her. Exploration and escape carry more weight than direct fighting. The castle's rooms offer clues, locked routes and hiding places, while the presence of another living creature gives Fiona someone to rely on in a threatening environment.

The player controls Fiona directly and gives Hewie commands. Calling him, asking him to investigate or sending him toward a pursuer can create an opening, but his cooperation depends on their relationship. Praising and caring for the dog makes that bond part of play rather than simply a story detail. Fiona's own movement consumes stamina, and exhaustion makes escape harder. A chase therefore asks for more than holding a direction: the player must judge the route, the companion's position and the resources left to keep moving.

When Fiona becomes overwhelmed, panic affects both her behaviour and the presentation, making an already dangerous pursuit more difficult to control. Hiding and using the environment can buy time, while items offer ways to recover or hinder an enemy. Director Kazuhiro Tsuchiya's team built a vulnerable protagonist whose limited means keep the emphasis on evasion. The game received a mixed critical response, with praise for its atmosphere and partnership alongside criticism of repetition. Its relationship between the pursued character and her dog remains its most recognisable idea.
